what: aide-memory@0.2.0 is already published to npm (2026-04-11) but is STALE — it contains pre-cleanup code including --scan, unbundled sources, and missing-deps bugs (chalk, fast-glob not listed). feature/phase-1 has significantly advanced beyond it (scan removed, pending-memories import, drift-repair, 18-setting public surface, test suite at 654 tests). Any next publish must bump PAST 0.2.0 — recommended 0.3.0 (breaking via --scan removal under pre-1.0 SemVer). Live 0.1.1 (2026-04-08) is the prior stable; 0.2.0 (2026-04-11) should optionally be deprecated via `npm deprecate aide-memory@0.2.0 "superseded by 0.3.0 — contained pre-release bugs"` after 0.3.0 publish. Verify before publish: `curl -s https://registry.npmjs.org/aide-memory | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.loads(sys.stdin.read()); print(list(d["versions"].keys()))'`.
why: Discovered when attempting to scope the minified-publish release — my proposal of 0.2.0 as next version was wrong because it's already live (with stale code). Critical for any future publish work. Separate from memory 151's full recommendation record because future version decisions will need this specific fact without loading the full context.
